The Shepherds have returned with another haul of cattle from the surface. In accordance with our instructions from Lord Felwil, we’ll separate healthy adult males from those who can be fodder for the Hellgrowth.

 The men will be carefully vetted to determine their ability to withstand the Growth Hormone derived from the new strain of Infernal Flora.

It is expected that at least 7 out of the first 10 will die, the surviving 3 will move on to the next round of hormones. Should any perish, we are instructed to scavenge the limbs that have achieved the most growth.

It is not expected that one male will survive every round of injections; rather, the orders inform us to expect upwards of 29 healthy adult males to create the construct; the fewer, the better for efficiency's sake.

Should this Iconostein, Felwil calls “Behemoth,” be successful, we are to report our success to him for the next phase of the project.

Welcome to the Crimson Moon's Summer Build!

This demo reflects the current state of team's development towards our First Playable milestone later this year. In this play session you will be slaying monsters, scavenging for gear, leveling your Nephilim, and more while exploring the first of the two areas we are building as part of this gate. 

Everything in the build, from difficulty to combat to systems, is being iterated on, making this a great time to step back and gather external input as we iterate in this next stretch.

Thank you for taking the time to play our game and share your feedback with us! We look forward to sharing our progress in the coming months.

- Team Metal

The session concludes at the end of the District, but feel free to continue exploring the next District to get a sneak peak of where the level will continue expanding.

The Scribe’s disciplinary action has kept me from a night’s rest for some time. I pored over the literature on Angels and couldn’t find anything to corroborate his theories. However, something I’ve read before caught my attention.

In the 6th passage of chapter 43 on Sergio’s Metaphysics of Being, something stuck out to me given the context of the scribe’s claims.

“Those who stood by the Divine maintained their formless purity and those who did not, crystallized into abominable transience.

The nature of the heavens could not allow for the Finite to taint the perfect Infinite.

He was the god of war, and he wanted nothing else but to be in conflict with a blade in his hand. While the other powers shaped Eden, he marched across it, and his Mahktens marched with him marauders and mercenaries who lived only for the next battle. It was the Lord of Perdition who began the War of the Gods, certain he could take the world step by step. He was wrong, but only just. When he was finally bound into the Abraxas Stone, the heavens themselves were left scarred. He has waited in the dark ever since, and waiting is the one thing he was never built for. The Mahktens were his faithful, less a people than an appetite, gathered from every war-torn corner of Eden. They fought the Lunitarians long after their god was sealed, and they lost. What became of the last of them, no chronicle agrees. They passed out of history and into the kind of story soldiers tell to frighten one another, which is perhaps the only afterlife a Mahkten would have wanted.

They call it the Sundering now: the war that taught Eden its gods could bleed. When it ended, the world wore new scars, places where the sky never quite closed, where the ground still remembers being torn. The Lunitarians counted it a victory as the world bled for their God.

They say that when the stone closed around him, the Lord of Perdition laughed. He had spent his whole existence hunting for an enemy who could not simply be beaten and discarded, an enemy worthy of forever. In the end, the seal gave him exactly his deepest desire. Whatever else it has taken from him, it has not touched his patience. He has all the time in the world now, and he means to spend it.

Of course I’ll remember. 
Even if easier to forget. 
I shall never forgive the Church for this day.
I renounce and study at Elk Grove Academy.

May every book bring memories of you
As you rest ever after in your tomb
--Mereda

I did not inform Renault that I would try to bind the Angel once it had taken over him; I knew he wouldn’t have agreed, but I was too close to let anything get in my way. Too many have died for me to get answers already.

Once I bound the Angel, I commanded Apothos to tell me why the Divine is silent. 

Aothos Spoke:

“Afflicted by the malady of eternity

What is taken must one day be returned.

In time, the Throne will Coil its Lord 

And the Serpent will reawaken.”

They do not serve the Divine. They serve the Throne itself. This faith-shattering revelation must not be lost. What we are told is a lie; the Divine hasn’t turned his back on us for our sins… he is dying.. Does The Holy Lineage know this?

I thought they was just takin’ the ones got sick at the tavern.
Piling ‘em in the streets.
Building somethin’.
But that weres just the start.
When the tavern sick was gone, they started knocking.
Knock, knock knocking.
Door to door they went. Always knocking.
I watched ‘em take Helene.
Sweet Helene, think she was seventeen this year.
Knock, knock knocking.
Watched her from me window, crouching dirt on me knees, as she swung her door open, eyes wide with relief.
The city guard, she thought.
But they weren’t right. Red veins like ivy crawled all up and down ‘em.
Knock, Knock knocking.
They took her screaming.
Thank gods never looked my way, but she screamed hell.

Two days later, she returned.
Knock, knock knocking on my door.
She won’t leave, won’t stop.
Just keep knock knock knocking.

She knows I’m in here. Knows I did nothing but watch.
Poor Helene. Of all of ‘em, why’d you have to come
Knock, knock knocking.
I think it’s time I just let you in

I was but a boy yesterday, when I accepted the Red Gift. The crowd stirred as the Prophet Felwyl spoke. His voice of honey, his words of promise and unification. The Eternal Garden awaits us all. A coming salvation that will unite all souls in perfect harmony. It was beautiful. It was…forever.

After the sermon, we queued and waited to accept his gift. It twilled and squirmed in my hand. Bitter on the tongue. But warm in the chest. I can already feel the transformation coming, teaching me that even a lord must kneel, and in kneeling, learn to serve.

I write this letter with my last eye, trembling in the wrist with excitement, barely able to wait 
to pluck the final gift from its cavity and fling it happily into the maw of my God.  
I write to say he came to me he came to me it’s true! All of it. He is real. Dreams are dreams 
of knowledge and wine. What is an eye to give when all an eye can see is the material realm 
and it is only in the dream that knowledge can be seen. 
One does not need eyes to see. One merely needs dreams.

In the hunt for Aegoroth, Eye of the Abyss, I grow closer. A resident from the Inn claims to have come across a most peculiar people. Just three days journey from here. To hear him say it, during his travels in the Armaea Hills he came across a small wooden structure, what he thought was a church. Upon closer inspection, he found the building empty. 

Being a storm coming, he decided to shelter for the night. It must have been the lightning that saved him--for he awoke startled by the flash and in that wisp of light, he found men standing all around him, spread about in a fanning circle, all watching him sleep, all with empty hollows where there should be eyes.

Just like that, the light passed and he was left in the dark. And when the next flash came-they were gone. It is said that devout followers relinquish their eyes to Aegoroth for just a glimpse of his flesh. Lunacy. Fanatics. Obviously. But still, a fantastic opportunity for a firsthand interview! They must know more about the lost legends of this fabled creature than any.  

I shall begin my journey tomorrow.

It appears the Lunitarian’s occupation of Gildenarch was far more interesting than I could have imagined. Their interest in the Abraxas Stones was no mere fall from grace; they were direct orders from the Holy Lineage themselves over 400 years ago. The irony that I was far more devout than my superiors at that time doesn’t surprise me. The slave morality they’ve instilled in their subordinates kept us from ambition, yet the Holy Lineage themselves have greater ambitions than perhaps even I, today. In some sense, I am doing Eden a service by destroying the veil. I can only imagine what those theocrats had in store for the realm with that kind of power.

It has long been a point of contention regarding the origins of the Lunitarian faith. The accepted canon is that it was established by The Holy Lineage around 333. If we consider the Sentinel Conflict of 234, the faith’s earliest adopters must have existed more than a century ago. After the Sentinels were eradicated and Emperor Alonious abdicated the Imperial Throne, the faith wrote the history books.

It is all about time, something which I have ample amounts of. Time for pain to fester, time for desperation to spread, and time for hopelessness to cloud judgment. Man is incapable of truly withstanding the weight of this world; their endless desire for a savior shall be their undoing.

 So I shall save these lost souls; they will have opportunity, industry, and hope. Lastly, but most importantly, something to hate. Each other.

 Fewyl is ready to begin planting the seeds, so to speak, the theology he’s prepared is a sound and almost convincing inversion of the Lunitarian’s premises on the Shattered Coil. I couldn’t have chosen a more ambitious monster to work with. I’ll have to keep my eye on him.

It is done. The humans have been erradicated. We'll take the tunnels the Spire and meet our Lord in the Ritual Chamber. 

Tonight, Eden dies.

I’ve returned from the company’s dinner. My efforts to influence the Archbishop have been unsuccessful; I may have to apply additional pressure to gain access to the Stones. He is not reliable, I am afraid; his skepticism may be thwarted by the Chapter’s desperation, but even then, he is far too stubborn. One door closes, and another opens, of course. I met the charismatic Cardinal Mathias this evening. As devout, if not more than the Archbishop, yet desperately hoping to see the city’s revival. If I can somehow replace the Archbishop with Mathias, I might yet have my way. Mathias wants to see the city thrive once again, and so it shall be. Nachtstahl Steel shall lead this effort. Then, I shall have what is mine.

Mon — Meat shipment is wrong. Wrong shape. Wrong color. Not asking what. 

Tue — Salt cellar half empty. Someone is taking salt down to the lower. Two stone of salt does not season prisoners. 

Wed — Heard them again last night. Below the cold room. Like a choir, but the wrong number of voices for the throats I know are down there. 

Thu — Fish boy gone. Said he was going down to fetch the morning's haul. Did not come up. Was told not to replace him. 

Fri — Cooking for forty. Feeding twelve. Where is the food going. I will not ask. I will not ask. I will not ask.

Monday. Fitting at Madame Auvern's at the Sixth Bell. Tea at Reverence Hall. The Devereaux woman is wearing crimson, of course she is, the woman has the imagination of a banker's wife. Sash for me, then; one cannot match.

Tuesday. The Cathedral Auxiliary, then dinner at the Haedriks. Edmund pleads his nerves and will not come. He has pled his nerves three weeks running. I am beginning to suspect his nerves know of nothing other than pleading.

Wednesday. Sat for my portrait. The painter remarked that the moon has been very red of late, and asked if I had noticed. I said the moon is not noticed if one is properly dressed.

Thursday. Lunch with Vivienne. She said two of her staff have given notice without explanation. I gave her mine. I have a girl from Pontoon Town who is grateful and quiet and has not yet had the chance to learn how to leave.

Friday. Confession. I lied about the usual things. Father Olm seemed distracted. I asked after his health. He said he had been sleeping poorly, and that the chapel candles were burning low.

The Eve. The Spire. Crimson sash. Eighth Bell. Carriage at the door.

I am told one must, on these occasions, smile.

Mr. Calder —

I have your note. I had it twice, in fact, the second hand-delivered, which I take to mean you wished to be sure I had read the first. I have read both. I write now from the cellar, where I am, as we speak, twenty-three years into the practice of selecting wine for households that pay better than yours.

The Gevreyne of '38: provenance correct. Vinified at Halt's Cross, eight years in my bin. Object if you must to my taste. Not to my certainty.

The Gilded Solera, vault-numbered — yes, I will tell you, I cannot recall ordering it. Yes, I will tell you, the manifest does not list it. I have had a bottle delivered without invoice before. I have not had one delivered without a man.

The Choir's Vintage. You are correct. None has been shipped from the Old Vineyards in twelve years. The bottles I have placed for the head table are bottles my master left me when I came up. There are eight. I have always known there were eight.

Yesterday there were seven. I counted them four times. I counted them with Pelham. I counted them with a candle and a chalk mark on the rack, the way a child counts. There were seven. I have neither slept nor eaten since.

This morning there are eight.

Pelham swears he has not touched them. I believe him. I cannot say I have always believed myself.

I will take responsibility for the list. The list is mine. I am not an old man yet, Calder, but I am old enough to know when a cellar has been entered, and I am old enough to know when it has been entered twice.

Pour from the right side of the head table first. I will decant the Choir's Vintage there myself.

And come down before the carriages arrive. I would like you to look at the rack with me.

— Master Auber

My Mereda,
I have no reason to believe this will find you. If I have learned one thing since they pulled me out of training it is that war, real war, is chaos. I have no doubt that it was created by the Infernal Legion. No rules, no order, just violence, blood, and the howls of the dying. 
I have seen men fall to their knees and beg for their mothers. I have watched thousands of men be cut down in front me. The crimson mist of their blood fills the air. I can still taste their blood on my tongue. 
This is all because of one demon. Valahk-Nor. They call him a general, but what even is that to the Infernal Legions? He’s just a bigger more deadly demon than the rest. I care not. I’m going to kill this demon spawn for taking me away from you. If it weren’t for him, I would have had that night with you under the willow. 
I am going to run my sword through Valahk-Nor's throat for you. I will drag his head back from this unholy place and present it to you as my amends for leaving. And then, I will take you in my arms and we will make up for the days and months we have lost, Mereda. My passion has only grown since I have been pulled away from you. It is all consuming for me. 
I  am off, the troops are marshalling. I know I said that tomorrow was a promise neither one of us could give, but I promise you, I will return and we will have our time under the willow.
I am forever truly yours,
Gallant

My Mereda,
Oh how many times have I tried to write this letter to you? How many times have I burned the pages for fear of being found by the Church? I know it has been years since you thought me dead. Since I was dead. But I thought about you every day since.
After we won the Battle of the Last Kingdoms, the Church took us in. We thought it was to reward us for fulfilling our sacred duty. But instead it was a trap. They tricked us and  walked us into our own abattoir. We were slaughtered before we could even draw our swords. I would like to tell you that I fought well and held on to the last, but I didn’t. I fell as quickly as the rest.
And yet, I write to you now. No, I am not some specter haunting you beyond death’s threshold. No, I am very much alive, resurrected. The angel who lives inside of me pulled me back from the cold darkness and gave me a second life. 
The Church isn’t sure what to do with me. "Gallow’s Wraith” they call me. I’ll take the moniker if it means I’m able to save the few of my brothers who still yet live. Strange as it may sound, I am trying to work with the Church. Getting them to stop hunting the Nephilim in exchange for our service and fealty to them. I’m trying to establish an Order. 
Please come join me. We could do this together. We will need your knowledge and your critical eye. The Church is overflowing with tomes that haven’t been touched for generations. You would love it here. 
I confess the years have done little to diminish what I feel for you. Please, join me and let us see what we can make of this new Order. Perhaps we shall even find a new willow tree.
Yours,
Gallant

My Mereda, with a heart that feels set aflame by Cain himself, I burn for your touch. My ears can hear nothing but your cooing laugh that flows past your lips like a joke only you will ever know. 
My angel tells me I am being foolish – of course I am. He tells me I should focus on my training. Why would I give even a fraction of my thought on that punishing, brutal, and cruel treatment, when I can close my eyes and see your form laid bare before me.
I have not been lucky in my young life, but finally winning you over to my passions and pulling you away from your books is my greatest fortune. You said we were doomed from the start, but I don’t care. I would fight through the infernal gates and slay a thousand souls to once again feel your body against mine. You may think we are doomed, but from the lingering taste of you upon my lips I know you don’t care either. 
The world, no, all of the heavens and hells are at war, my love. Tomorrow is a promise neither of us can keep. But tonight, my dearest, tonight I can promise that if you meet me under our old willow tree I will burn the heavens themselves with my passion for you. My hands have no purpose if not to hold you. My heart has no reason to beat if not near you --
My commander enters, I must go. Be with me tonight.
I am forever truly yours 
Gallant

My dear Mr. Moore — if I may presume the address —

You will forgive a letter from a man you may not recall having met. We were introduced at the Cathedral Auxiliary’s spring concert, two years past, by Master Felwyl. I do not expect the moment was memorable to you. The fault was mine.

My daughter, Vespera Halhurst, has spoken for weeks now of an understanding between yourself and herself.

I have written that sentence six times. It has not improved.

She is a vivid girl. In her years at the Academy, she has brought home many enthusiasms: poets, causes, philosophies, flowers pressed between borrowed books. Most passed before supper grew cold.

This one has not passed.

She has named the garden. She has named the hour. She has described, with some firmness, the jewel she believes would befit the occasion. When asked whether she possesses any letter from you, she says she has better than a letter, and will show it when I stop treating her as a child.

I did not press her further.

Should any part of this prove true, you would find me the readiest blessing in Gildenarch. You would also find, at your disposal, such endowment as remains within my house. Wassinger & Stoke have my instructions.

Should it prove — as I suspect it must — that my daughter has mistaken courtesy for affection, and affection for intention, I beg you to consider this letter unsent. I have asked no answer. I have imposed no obligation. The matter shall remain the private foolishness of one humble household.

I shall not see you at the Gala. I had not the standing to be invited. Vespera, however, has been beside herself all morning. She has dismissed two gowns, wept over a sash, and asked three times whether a man such as yourself prefers rubies to diamonds.

I told her I would not know.

She laughed at that. Kindly, I think.

I shall be at home tonight, hoping for word from my daughter, and dreading it in equal measure.

With every regard, and every deference,

-Cornelius Halhurst

My dear Wensleigh,

Two candles, and the second already crooked. You will forgive the haste. I write quickly because this evening, when it comes, will be very long.

You are a rare student. I do not say this to flatter you. I say it because the saying has become rare. Most who pass through my hall admire the lantern, and the pleasing circle of light it permits them. You have always been of a different garden, most content at the edges of the light.

I will speak briefly tonight. The Cardinal will speak longer. Our Patron will speak last, and the wine will be very fine, and you will be bored, and that is right and good.

After the toasts — when the older guests find the air heavy and retire to their carriages — find me. There is a smaller gathering for the few who have taken the trouble to look further. I have argued for your inclusion. The argument was not difficult. It rarely is, with you.

Wear something you can move in. Pin nothing to your collar that you would mourn.

Yours, in faith and in the better light to come,
 F.

Why am I seeing this?

The mogul assures us that his work will yield promising results, and the Archspire will take full credit for what is to come. A deal too good to be true, if you ask me. I hope to be pleasantly surprised.

Solomon — 

You ask if I have the stomach. I have eaten venison while a poacher hung dripping from my rafters, keeping time with the strings. I do not lack stomach. 

The keep is yours. Take it down to the sea-stones if it pleases you. The lower wards too — I'm told the air there is rich, and that the men who survive long enough develop a most remarkable patience. 

You offer me red, and long red years to drink it. I accept. I would have signed for the offer alone, without the keep — but you are a man of style, and I shall not deprive you of the pleasure of payment. 

I'll be at the Aemar after the second course. Have something young ready. The first hunger, I'm told, is a memorable thing. 

— H. Caldwell

Solomon, your absence at the gathering has aroused suspicion among the Patriarchs and Matriarchs of the other clans. I do not know what it is you’re doing in Velchoria, but I must remind you of the Pact. Cain is dead, and it is better he remains that way; we’ve no desire to go to war against the Church or all of Eden, for that matter. Without mankind, we have no cattle, and as long as Cain can’t reach us, we are free to use his blood as we see fit. We have something good going on; other clans do not want you jeopardizing it for your religious nonsense.

Lastly, I’d be remiss not to remind you that you still owe Clan Telvaught our blade Scirax. If you do not return it to us, we may come to collect it.

Tabitha, 

I hope this letter finds you well 
For it may be my last
You were right my dear
Nothing comes without its price
Those bastards did something to the drink
It squirms inside me

It speaks.

I can hear everything it says.
I can see everything it wants.
All I want is to come home to you my dear
But what it wants--
Yes. Maybe I should.

Yes, of course. I should come home to you straight away.
This warmth, this growth, I must share it with you.
I shall fill your heart with love. The love you have always asked me for.
And through the scarlet embrace of the red bloom, we shall be together forever.
Tabitha, my dear. I shall be home soon.

The Dry Rot King, his people called it before the name was the last word any of them could still speak.

The Saedrics were his people: keepers of the old groves, who counted their years in harvests rather than kings. When their god began to rot in the dark, something of him reached back through the roots and into them. They did not die. They dried.
Now they are the Rot Kin, and they tend the forest the way grief tends a grave. The stone was never a prison so much as a wound stitched shut. It holds a god, but it does not heal him and it does not silence him. The wardens who guard it report the same thing across centuries,the longer he is kept, the less of E'frae remains, and the more of the rot answers in his place.

Where his influence reaches, the land does not burn or drown. It simply gives up. Leaves brown on a windless day. Timber crumbles though no rain has touched it. Animals lie down and do not rise again. It is not death, exactly, death is an ending, this is a slow forgetting of how to be alive.

The Inquisition brought in someone interesting this last night. They were indeed a heretic but not of the Reborn, no this was a man who practiced the old ways. He claims to commune with the god E'frae. Though worth noting he claims this is NOT the Lord of the Wild from the Island of Saedrys but instead his corpse he so zealously called "The Dry Rot King". He claims this entity slumbers deep beneath Gildenarch, total nonsense but heresy none the less. We will let the Inquisitor decide his fate.

The Karsivite pagans are a strange sort, not that any aren’t addled. The Conversions handled by the Orthodoxy are not ideal, but our sects are aligned enough, I suppose. Remember that mission in Ulsvelled 4 winters ago? Where we met with the tribes and provided food and supplies. They had a blacksmith amongst them, a strange one at that. Apparently he was an outsider, “raised by wolves” -quite literally. Well, that same tribe was the one that rose up and had to be put down by the Crusaders. It was only after that the murders among the Orthodoxy had begun. I heard a rumor that the vampire the Nephilim were sent to kill was that blacksmith. Even more insane to suggest, but the Nephilim have allegedly conscripted a new smith from those lands who is a vampire. I can’t confirm any of this but do understand that suspicion of pagans isn’t unfounded; we’ve been to their lands and see what madness occurs; it's only fitting Nephilim would take pity on them.

The South Bed. Asters opened on the eleventh of the Fifth Month. Last year was the twentieth. Year before that, the twenty-second. In thirty years I never seen them open so early.

Roses on the West Border. No rust. Not one leaf. Rust come every June since '79, every year. None this year. I should be pleased. I am not.

The Eastern Plot. Three rows of bulbs come up that I never put down. White, narrow at the bottom, fluted at the top, with a kind of tongue between the petals. I asked Halt at the apothecary. He never seen them. I asked the man at Vellgrove Press. He never seen them. I borrowed a book on Velchorian flora from the Library. The book don't know them either. They opened on Tuesday and they have not closed since.

The North Bed. There is a worm in the soil that don't answer to lime. I tried lime. I tried fire. I tried salt. The worm is in a jar on my bench and it has not stopped moving. When I look at it long enough, it stops looking like a worm.

The Conservatory. A vine of a kind I do not know, putting out a flower I cannot put a name to. It come up between the floorstones, where there is no soil. It is rooted in stone. I cut it on Monday. It was back on Wednesday and longer. The flower opens at dusk and turns to the south doors. The first hour it has no smell. The second hour it smells of a dressed hare.
I asked Bevan to keep the south doors locked tonight. He said he will. He is a good boy.
I will be on the grounds for the Gala. The lanterns want lighting. The torches on the carriage path want lighting. After that I will sit in my shed and watch the south doors.
— Marn

The first question one must ask when inquiring on the true inception point of knowledge, is 
the question of dreams. Where do they come from? Are they merely our internal 
hallucinations by sleep? Or is it a thread dripping through the ether, providing knowledge 
from the other side? From some one or some thing on the other side of the veil. 
I have been with the Aegorothians for a fortnight and they have me questioning my 
preconceptions.  
Lunatics, maybe. But these men and women willingly gave their eyes to their god. Plucked 
one by one as grapes for the Eye of the Abyss. And not a single one claims that they cannot 
see. 
They say it started with dreams. Dreams of knowledge. Dreams of sight. In these dreams, 
they see impossible things and eventually, Aegoroth himself. They describe large, 
magnificent wings and many, many eyes. Blue irises. And brown. Every kind. 
Could it be that all this time true knowledge came from the other side traveling through our 
dreams. Forbidden knowledge from a gracious god.  
And if it is true, I wonder, will he visit me?

The period following the establishment of the Crimson Concordat was tumultuous, as it was implemented immediately across Velchoria without question. The enforcers of the agreement were the first Nephilim conscripted, led by the Knight Commander Gallant Alexander. The Order would accompany clergy and priesthood within Velchoria and protect Missionaries in Armaea or Karsiv. Conversion within the Empire was relatively peaceful, with the exception of those who fled to the countryside of the Treveyan Highlands and actively resisted all attempts. A few skirmishes broke out among the Nephilim, laying the groundwork for resistance abroad. 

These Apostates would eventually be given no other choice than to die by the blade. The Knight Commander himself famously led the slaughter south of Saedrys, where the village of Kambrook refused to turn over their Nephilim. 

Throughout the world, Nephilim belonging to the Oath of Moonlight, called Specters, would assassinate Nephilim in foreign lands to prevent the Empire’s rivals from harboring them. Exception being the Karsivite Orthodoxy, who had gone out of their way to turn Nephilim over to the Velchorian Church before Specters arrived.

To this day, the Apostate Hunts still continue but have largely died down. The period we colloquially refer to as the Hunts have long passed, but its scars still remain.

The time has come, Mathias. We have belayed our response long enough. The disorder and chaos that we’ve allowed to fester within the city has now justified extreme action.  

In fact, the people hunger for it. They yearn for the strength of the iron hand. 

Even the worst heresy, sometimes, is an act in service to the greater good.  And make no mistake, there is no greater good without evil.  No advancement without destruction. No immortality without death.  

The death of others, at least.

As prefect of the Doctrine, you've done your part, your Emminence. Now we will do ours.

The people have asked for the touch of the iron hand.

Now, Mathias, we will give them what they want. 

-Solomon.

The wanted criminal Lotte Ananta has been arrested after a break-in at the Archspire Cathedral this weekend. You can cross him off your list of troublemakers in this city; the charges alone will do him in, but the poor sucker got cursed after grabbing an artifact from the Church’s vaults.

Looks like his "magical abilities" didn’t spare him from this one.

They told me I was here for killing my brother. I was. I would do it again, and the priest wept, and I laughed, and they put me in the dark for it. 

The dark was the kindest thing that ever happened to me. 

In the dark something began to grow in my chest. I do not mean the bloom — that came later. I mean a knowing. A quiet. The first quiet I have ever had. They feed me bread that tastes of rot, and it tastes of welcome. 

The Sister came today and asked if I was ready. I said yes. She kissed my mouth and left a seed inside. 

I am being chosen. I have never been chosen for anything before.

This is the sixth time those nutters have come knocking on my door at odd hours. The gall to proselytize such absurdities to Divine fearin' folk in Gildenarch of all places.  Not that the Archspire cares much anymore, unless it hurts their coffers.

Divine take 'em all. Them cultists and the Archspire cloth as well.

This one claimed to know nothing even after we broke his hands. We asked after his brother, but he would not give him up. Then we started on his feet. Then his tongue.  

Eventually, we broke him. Or thought we had. 

He feigned cooperation, and because he could no longer speak, motioned for a quill and parchment to be put in his hands for a signed confession.  

We gave him a quill, but the moment the inks were put before him, he smiled bloodily and dashed the ink in the guard's eyes. 

He managed to kill one of the inquisitors before he was put down. An ugly business. 

His brother has yet to be found.

This one’s beyond me; I’ve no idea what Gallant sees in that cretin. He’s actually gone and conscripted the thief from Archspire, for who knows what reason. He arrived at Shoreditch this last evening and demanded to see him. He looked the freak up and down and asked the guards to clear the room. After a few moments passed, he emerged and invoked the Rite of Conscription. Could it be the rumors about the thief are true? That his spirit can leave his body? Considering the state he’s in now, I’d imagine that ability might be useful.

Though man yet remains on this earth, we live in dread for how much longer. A new race walks among us, towering giants of incredible strength, agility, and innate tallents for sorcery and angelic foresight. They are in every way superior to us and yet do not know their nature. As mankind rebuilds we must live alongside beings who have known nothing but war and posesses talents that far exceed our own. Though some have pleged their service to rebuilding efforts other have taken to criminality, banditry or mercenary work. Most terrible is the tragedy of Saedrys where a Nephilim appeared to have gone "feral" and burnt what was left of the city to the ground. These creatures must be controlled or expelled from the realm, their freedom threatens our safety and we must seek any means to qwell their potential for destruction.

Toby, Hux, Magda, if any of you find this, I made it past Ramshorn, but the whole place has gone to hell. That madness we saw in Shoredtich has shaken up the town too. Folks been out here slaughtering each other its a mad house. Truth be told its been a cakewalk to escape with all of the commotion, but its too dangerous for me to stay. 

I’m going to scale the mountains outside Ramshorn and catch the first ship to Armaea. Screw Lotte, he can bloat and rot wherever the hell the Lunitarians took him. If any of you find this, please seek me out in Nachtendale or Belwayne; wherever we can get far away from Velchoria is where we’ll set up shop.

Tomas, my love — 

Your last reached me Tuesday. I've read it three times. The hand wasn't yours. I know your hand — eight years of it. The loops don't crowd like that, and you have never once spelt my name with the second N. 

Tell me you wrote it. Tell me your wrist is hurt and one of the kinder ones wrote for you. Tell me anything and I'll believe it, only write back in your own hand. 

I went to the gates yesterday with bread. The new Sister wouldn't take it. No visitors to the lower wards, she said. She wouldn't look at me. 

Lily asks for you every night. Write me. Write me in your own hand and I'll burn this. 

— Your Anya

Tuesday. Botanical Studies, third hour. Eight of us, two missing — Wynn says it's the cough going around, but I never met anyone who liked Wynn enough to tell her where they actually were.

Master Felwyl brought a new specimen today. He carried it himself, which he never does. A small thing in a glass dome. Pale pink, with red veins. He said the name in old Lunitarian and I didn't catch it. I'll ask Cora. Cora always remembers.

He let us each look. Up close it pulses, very softly, like it is breathing. Master Felwyl said this was not breathing. He said it was simply sap. He smiled when he said it.

It is a little ugly. The stem is too white. But the flower is, I must admit, the loveliest thing I have ever seen. When I smelled it, my mouth watered, which is silly. I keep thinking about it. I keep thinking about it the way I would think about a boy.

Vauron —

I am sending this to your townhouse, and I trust you will read it in your dressing-room before the carriage. Read it before you put on your gloves.

I have eight cases now, perhaps nine. The presentation is alike in each, and like nothing in the texts at my disposal.

An elevation of mood unaccounted for by circumstance. A wasting of the flesh that will not answer to appetite, which is in every case strong. A warmth and brightness of the complexion — one of my patients, a girl of seventeen, was good enough to call it a lit lamp behind the cheek, and I have not improved upon her phrase. The pulse hurried, near a hundred, even at rest. Sleep undisturbed. The spirits buoyant.

None complain of pain. This troubles me more than pain would.

I have had word from a colleague in Pontoon Town of the like in working men and women. I am told the Cathedral Auxiliary's clinic in the Mill Ward has seen perhaps a dozen this season among the poor. The same cheerfulness. The same hunger. The same light beneath the skin.

The Gala, my friend, will gather every ward of the city under a single roof. Old Money. New Money. Faculty. Clergy. Service staff drawn from districts they would not otherwise be permitted to enter. If this affliction passes from one body to another — and I am not yet prepared to commit to the if — then tonight is a pile of kindling into which we are placing several thousand small flames at once.

I ask you, as a friend, to look.

Look at the wrists, where the skin is thin. Look at the eyes when the candle is between you and the patient; the gleam will be unmistakable if one knows to look for it. Look at who eats, who only seems to eat, and who refuses with thanks. Watch especially for those who praise the wine and do not swallow.

Should you mark it in three guests — three, not two — withdraw from the room. Find me in the second-floor library. Bring whom you must. Tell no one why.

I have not yet a name for what this is. I know what it is not. It is not anything I was taught to recognise.
— M.

We're running low on provisions. No help is coming. Trapped in here with...him...Viktyr. Damn him! This is all his fault.

There's nothing to eat in here but the vermin that live in this cave. I'm sick of dried rat. The bat isn't so bad, but I think it's making us sick...

I miss my home. I miss my stream where I could fish for hours. I miss my garden where  I grew my prize-winning gourds. I'm making myself hungry...

Why did I sign up for this? Why did I let Viktyr convince me this was the right thing to do, knowing what we were up against?

Not much time left. I'm so hungry. I hope he dies first. So hungry...I'm...

We’ve received a request from the Knights of the Crimson Moon. Get this: they want to allow a Pagan Artifact from Karsiv in the halls of the Sanctus Clypeus to accommodate their blacksmith. This is not only absurd, it's literal heresy a violation of the faith. That Gallow’s Wraith is using the Concordat to test the limits of what is allowed within Velchoria. Excuse my outburst in this letter, but do let it sway you in your decision to grant this request.

What a cruel and undeserved fate, oh beautiful E’frae. Whose green ran through the earth, whose voice was whispered among the wind, and whose love gave rise to life every spring.

 I mourn your loss, great father of the wild, but I cannot join you in the Rot. I will journey far from these lands to the region of Western Armaea. Far from the Church’s clutches, I will plant your seed and tend to it as your wisdom tended to my soul.

The Saedric memory will live on even in this darkened age. Farewell, my father; I will carry you with me in all things I do.

What's reborn can be rekilled. Remember that, you fools. 

It's the cult that brought this down on all of us. I'd wager anything.

It was only me that ran. 

It’s important I write that here, so it’s recorded. I’d want no stench of desertion to be levied against the others, who fought bravely to a man. 

Their names should be clean, unlike mine—Daerun Bogmire, as it’s recorded in the sentry lists. A name, even bad as it is, that I couldn't live up to. 

Or maybe I did live up to it.  To run is in my name.

What does heaven look like, I wonder? Or mayhap it’s hell I should be thinking on. 

Soon I’ll know. The cut is deep, but that’s not what I’m afraid of. It’s the bite. The bite worries me. This bite that gives me frenzied thoughts. 

It’s not too long now afore I go. I feel it rising, like a fever. Please forgive me.     

I seen the walking bones. I knew them when they held flesh. Good men, some of them. Bad men, others. But as bones they are made equal as never they were in life. They are the damned. As soon am I.  

Or am already. 

Goodbye. 

The Bogmire name dies with me.  Good riddance.

COOKIES, MOBILE IDs, AND SIMILAR TECHNOLOGIES

We may use cookies, web beacons, mobile analytics and advertising IDs, and similar technologies to operate our websites, games, and apps to help collect data, including usage data, identifiers, and device information.

What are cookies and similar technologies?

Cookies are small text files placed by a website and stored by your browser on your device. A cookie can later be read when your browser connects to a web server in the same domain that placed the cookie. The text in a cookie contains a string of numbers and letters that may uniquely identify your device and can contain other information as well. This allows the web server to recognize your browser over time, each time it connects to that web server.

Web beacons are electronic images (also called single-pixel or clear GIFs) that are contained within a website or email. When your browser opens a webpage or email that contains a web beacon, it automatically connects to the web server that hosts the image (typically operated by a third party). This allows that web server to log information about your device and to set and read its own cookies. In the same way, third-party content on our websites (such as embedded videos, plug-ins, or ads) results in your browser connecting to the third-party web server that hosts that content. We also include web beacons in our email messages or newsletters to tell us if you open and act on them.

How do we and our partners use cookies and similar technologies?

We, and our analytics and advertising partners, use these technologies in our websites, and games to collect personal data (such as the pages you visit, the links you click on, and similar usage information, identifiers, and device information) when you use our services, including personal data about your online activities over time and across different websites or online services.[1] This data is used to store your preferences and settings, enable you to sign-in, analyze how our websites and apps perform, track your interaction with the site or app, develop inferences, deliver and tailor interest-based advertising, combat fraud, and fulfill other legitimate purposes. We and/or our partners also share the data we collect or infer with third parties for these purposes. For more information about the third-party analytics and advertising partners that collect personal data on our services, please see the “Our Disclosure of Personal Data” section of this Statement.

We do not knowingly use, or allow use of, data from users under 16 years of age or data collected from our child-directed games and experiences to deliver and tailor interest-based advertising.

What controls are available?

There are a range of cookie and related controls available through browsers, gaming platforms, and elsewhere. See the “Choice and Control of Personal Data” section below for details.

A heater shield carried by Covenant Clerics, the warrior-priests of the Crusader corps.

The cleric raises it against demons and dissenters alike; in the Church's reckoning, the difference between the two is a matter of confession.

A heater shield issued to Velchorian foot soldiers, faced in plain steel and trimmed in tarred leather.

Weather-worn but serviceable; the Empire issues them in a single grade and replaces them only when the rim splits past the boss.

A magnificent shield forged in honor of Gildenarch.

The magnificant rams of the Treveyan Highlands have long inspired the city of Gildenarch since the days before the city's founding.

No matter what changes, some truth yet remains.

A round aegis of gold and silver, two phoenix wings spread around a central sunburst.

Forged in Belwayne, where the phoenix is both heraldry and religion.

The Order keeps a small consignment for the Nephilim who came up through that city's halls.

A shield carried by Nephilim who refused the Crimson Concordat and lived long enough to need one.

Most were taken from the dead at the close of the first Apostate Hunts.

The few that were not are still in the field, and the Order does not press inquiries.

A shield of woven antler and root, knotted by the Stagkin in better times.

Their god has since begun to rot. The Rotkin still carry these shields; the antlers crumble and the roots no longer hold green leaf, but they say a shield need not live to defend its bearer, only remember its bearer's god.

A smoldering shield wielded by the extinct Mahkten Marauders. Bestial warriors in service to The Lord of Perdition.

In times of old, when the Coil was yet whole, war dominated the lands of Eden, and none were more adept than Mahkteah's devoted.

A tower shield bearing the heron of the Velchorian throne.

Carried by Sovereign Sentries in the halls of the imperial court.

The herons were once the only banner the Empire flew; now they fly beneath the Lunitarian moon, and the Sentries say nothing about it.

A tower shield bearing the sigil of the Crimson Concordat, issued to Nephilim of the Order.

The bond between Church and Order is rendered in steel and hung from the bearer's arm, carried by some as a vow honored and others as a debt remembered.

A wooden shield, weather-worn and softened by moss along its grain.

Salvaged from the bodies of conscripted militia who fell in the city's first night, before the Order arrived and the dying stopped being counted.

An accursed shield, once thought to be lost to legend.

The Revenant of Gildeus haunted depths of Gildenarch, watching over the forgotten dead buried under the Church's occupation.

An ancient shield integral to Lunitarian history, both feared and respected.

The Holy Lineage drew a clear delineation between the Lunar Sentinels and the Church.

The Sanctus Zealot enforced the New Order.

An ornate shield issued to knights who stood watch over the Archspire Cathedral.

Immaculate, and functional. The empire spent a good deal of coin when the Church demanded it.

Shield forged for Champions. Nephilim heroes from the Armaean citystate of Litinstang.

The rare few Nephilim who have proven themselves loyal to Litinstang are protected from Lunitarian law.

The Lunar Sentinels harken to a time before Lunarin's ascendance to the Divine Throne.

Any mentions of Lunarin worship before the Church are considered a vile heresy, attracting great skepticism and condemnation towards anyone "seeking to revive ancient knowledge" now considered outdated.

The shield of the vampire clan Telvaught.

Vampire Clans engage in ideological conlicts no better than humanity.

Clan Telvaught knew this well, and was always prepared for battle against their kin.
Amulet of the Vow of Retribution

Grants the Absolution in Ice boon. 

A final gift from the vanquished Dragon-God, a primordial ice to cleanse the soul.

Grants the Aegis of Frost boon. 

The heavily armored Aegis wields such strength that merely blocking an attack can damage foes.

Grants the Aftershock Technique boon. 

When Prometra fell, a giant crater formed. The Infernal Legion developed this technique in remembrance of the first fallen.

Grants the Ashen Verdict boon.

By this instrument, the fires of the wicked shall be turned against them. None may stand against the power of the divine.

Grants the Blessed Momentum boon. 

Stasis is death. Movement is life.

Grants the Brand of Judgement boon.

When whispers of a heretical cult reached the Lunitarian Church, they responded by sending the heavy hand of the Grand Inquisitor.

Grants the Chalice of Conquest boon.

The first vampires took eight sips from the Dark Lord's Chalice, whereupon their still hearts raced with a stolen vigor, newly sustained by the vitality of others.

Grants the Cleansing Conflagration boon.

A pariah turned member of the pack, Gajov dispels the coldness within by the fires of his forge.

Grants the Consecrated Draught boon.

Norunddir is home to the strongest drink, brewed to stave off the frost of ever-winter. The silver concoction burns the throat and speeds the heart.
Grants the Crown of Cinders boon.

Grants the Death Ward boon.

This gilded phylactory was found in a looted long barrow in the Helden Steppes. The sigils are in no known language to have ever been spoken there.

Grants the Defiant Vigor boon.

The vampires of Clan Moore are said to be almost impossible to kill. Legends tell that a single tincture of their blood may imbue a relic with super-restorative powers, though this is unconfirmed in the eyes of the Church.

Grants the Divine Endurance boon. 

As the Lord Taketh, so does He give. This trinket was found in the hold of a ship wrecked upon the beaches of Greighton Bay. According to the Church documents, it provides grace to the cup-bearer in direct proportion to the suffering endured.

Grants the Divine Focus boon.

A blind priest from the Drakefell Woods fasted and prayed that his sight be returned. It never was. Instead, he starved to death. The necklace he wore about his neck was kept and later found to have taken on strange properties. Though the priest never regained his sight, none may hide their wickedness from the eyes of the Lord.

Grants the Divine Reservoir boon.

Sister Fae Lake is said to be bottomless. Water drawn from its murky depths on the solstice is evaporated in the sun by monks, leaving a residue behind that contains mystical properties.
Grants the Edict of Condemnation boon

Grants the Enduring Rage boon.

Legends speak of tiny, hidden totems that can be secreted in the armor of doomed warriors which prevents them from feeling fear in the face of a lost cause. So powerful is this magic said to be that even a warrior with mortal wounds cannot be convinced to die.

Grants the Enduring Vow boon.

In breaking his vow of obedience, the fallen angel Prometra has lost his place in the Angelic Choir. It’s said that to find a feather of one of his wings is to be granted special powers.

Grants the Executioner’s Reward boon.

According to Church documents, Mox Piet was the most prolific executioner in the Velchorian Isles, and during his long life performed more than 700 confirmed executions for three generations of royalty. At the age of ninety-three, his final execution was himself. Aferward, his sword was melted down and drabs of dull steel were sold as relics.

Grants the Extra Supplies boon.

Forged to aid the Lost Legion, this little gimrack was created as a balance against the whole bounty of the Garden of Paradise. In this it failed, but it still has its uses.

Grants the Font of Conviction boon.

Belief is half the battle.

Grants the Font of Light boon.

Long have there been legends of ancient relicts, used by the Lunitarian Church to channel angelic grace to those who need it most. The Relict of Recovery is one such, and its bearer is suffused with the healing Light of the holy Divine.

Grants the Frostbound Charge boon.

Painfully cold to the touch, this small sliver of ice never melts, no matter how warm the day, and is often taken for a jewel by those who don’t know better

Grants the Frostbrand Seal boon.

So cold it burns the flesh of the unworthy, leaving a permanent brand upon the skin. Only a Nephilim can touch it and be unmarked.

Grants the Hardened Fury boon.

Around the doomed churches of Quorum were placed special guard stones. After most of the churches burned, these failed stones retained the heat of the fire, and to this day are passed around in remembrance of that tragedy.

Grants the Healing Hands boon.

An old sawbones pressed into duty after the battle of Helden Steppes was found to have the lowest mortality among his patients of any doctor. He credited his luck with clean hands, but others found reason to credit the amulet he wore, cast from white silver.

Grants the Holy Fire Aegis boon.

Some fires, once lit, cannot be put out.

Grants the Hunter's Strike boon.

It is a rare thing to kill a dragon. Even small shards of dragon horn are highly valuable and sought after by relic hunters.
Grants the Judgment of Winter boon

Grants the Last Bastion boon.

Once used as currency when gold was scarce, bricks from the ruins of Treveyan’s Keep have been scattered to the four winds.

Grants the Last Light boon.

A vampire has a complex relationship with the sun. In certain ancient tomes there are stories of special totems which might ease the daylight path of those who feast on blood. When carried by beings of the light, these totems grant other advantages.

Grants the Martyr's Gift boon.

A priest named Olan Blooded died by pagan hands during the second siege of Acktin. So brave was he that he was given a martyr’s burial, and a medallion to wear upon his chest. Two centuries later, the grave was looted, and the medallion stolen. Where it is now no one knows.

Grants the Oathbound Arts boon. 

Born of forbidden blood, The Knights of the Crimson Moon swear an oath to atone for the sins of their father in the blood of the Church’s enemies.
Grants the On a Pale Horse boon.

Grants the Radiant Fortitude boon.

An amulet forged to recognize the Divine’s triumph over the Demiurge as the start of a new era.

Grants the Resounding Flames boon.

A hardened ring that passes fire to all it touches. Passed down by an ancient cleric who claimed to travel through the gates of Infernus and return unharmed.
Grants the Scourge of the Unfaithful boon

Grants the Seal of Blight boon.

Members of the Reborn resent the Lunitarian Church and their Divine for undoing the old world and only through the Red Bloom can they unify all bodies into one again.

Grants the Seal of Flame boon.

The Lost Legion of Infernus believe that only by combining the eight fires of their region, can they burn the world anew.

Grants the Second Wind boon.

On the shores of Quidar Lake lived a pagan people long known to possess an affinity for communing with elementals. Before their villages were burned and their lands salted.
Grants the Shield of Many boon

Grants the Soulbound Might boon.

It is said that even mighty must fall. But it need not be this day.

Grants the Trial by Flame boon.

Long ago, in the blasted lands of Kah’s Spine, the pagans found a strange metal in the base of a crater. For a thousand years, this nugget was passed down, hammered into many forms. Always, it seemed to bring sickness and death to those closest to it. But finally, when the metal was stamped with the sigils of a great sorcerer, its power was harnessed.
Grants the Trial of Suffering boon
Grants the Trial of the Fallen boon

Grants the Unyielding Pyre boon.

Not all who burn are consumed.
Grants the Vow of Retribution boon
Grants the Zeal of the Faithful boon

Behold the Archspire Cathedral, from which Gildenarch owes its namesake. Once a vibrant seat of devotion for the Lunitarian faith, it has now succumbed to an insidious curse, ushered in by secrecy, fear, and unchecked ambitions.
Behold the Godsreach Spire, the baleful tower of unknown origin that drills through the heart of our realm. What vile secrets dwell within its halls have yet to be seen, until now…

Beyond the doors of St. Uriel's chapel, where the dead prowl blight-ridden streets, lies the treacherous path to the Archspire Cathedral. One fraught with tragedies that precipitated the demonic siege.
Confront Felwyl, The Ascended to regain control of the 3rd Abraxas stone and stop Solomon from piercing the veil.
Deep below Shoreditch, an ancient chamber is discovered. The Dead God Mahkteah, Lord of Perdition, is awakened.
Easy difficulty significantly lowers health and damage from enemies and is intended as an introductory experience.
Enter Gildenarch and battle through random districts to reach the World Boss and acquire an Abraxas Stone.
Feral Vampires, Demons, Undead, and Imps detected.
Hone your combat abilities and test your equipment against a variety of enemies from the game.
In the northernmost section of Gildenarch lies the city's Gilded Ward. Where mighty walls, once kept out those deemed undesirable, now hold back the infested pits of the Infernal Realm.

The Industrial Heart of Grimhaven was central to Gildenarch's revival and its demise. Weaponized divisions became the driving force behind the spear hurled towards the heavens.
The catacombs of the Southern Ward run deep, holding secrets obscured by horrors and ancient traps.
The decrepit former home of the City Garrison, the Shoreditch Wall Tower now houses a rising battalion of demons and its resurrected General.
The former home of Solomon Moore holds the secrets to his magic and whereabouts.
The site of investigation and experimentation with hellgrowth, Elk Grove Academy is now overrun with abominations and cultists alike.
Undead, Brutes, Captains, and Abominations detected.

Warp into a hell rift to battle waves of the infernal legion. Only brave and skilled Nephilim are likely to survive.

What was once a small fishing hamlet of a forgotten name is now the Southern Ward of Gildenarch. Formally established under Lunitarian occupation with the construction of the city’s famous Archspire Cathedral.
What was once interred for fear of its incendiary truth has brought the world to its knees. In the Graveyard of the Arschpire Cathedral lies the Dead God E'frae, the Dry Rot King.
With two Abraxas Stones in hand, confront the dead god Aegoroth for the 3rd stone and stop Solomon from piercing the veil.

A Lunitarian execution blade, drawn only at the close of an Apostate Hunt.

Forged from the swords seized at the signing of the Crimson Concordat.

The Church's ledgers name every Nephilim who has carried it; the ledgers do not name the apostates it has put down.

A Sanctus Pyre, its blade hacked to a charred spike and the wielder presumably with it.

The thorn-halo and the saint's tear remain unscathed; the rest is soot and rust.

A wandering pilgrim will sometimes carry one in penance for a village no record remembers.

A beautiful longsword wielded by the Phoenix Paladins of Belwayne.

The Armaean City-State of Belwayne is famous for their Phoenix heraldry and ornate weapons and armor.

A blade forged for Champions, Nephilim heroes from the Armaean city-state of Litinstang.

The rare few Nephilim who have proven themselves loyal to Litinstang are protected from Lunitarian law.
A blessed shield of lost renown once hung within the Chapel of Uriel. Said to sanctify the grounds within its presence, this blessing has waned over time.

A broadsword pulled from the dead. Broken, pitted, and past serviceable repair.

Recruits who cannot afford their own blade make do with these.

Most of the breaks are old; most of the bodies are older.

A broadsword salt-bitten by the Treveyan grave-roads and re-bound for resale.

The smiths who turn these around know better than to ask whose blade it was; the men who buy them know better than to ask whether the answer is one name or several.

A corrupted blade forged from the bones of an ancient beast.

The tragic corruption of the ancient Stagkin is felt today through their wicked weaponry.

Although brittle in appearance, these swords are anything but.

A crude single-bit axe sharpened on whatever stone the wielder could find.

Favored by highwaymen of the Treveyan roads and the press-ganged crews of the Velchorian docks. Most are stolen; the rest are paid for in stolen coin.

A gilded saber-glaive carried by the honor guards of the Aurullian sun-courts.

Forged for ceremony before war, the dragon-scroll on the blade is older than the iron beneath it.

The guards have carried these long enough that the families of the courts have forgotten which served whom.

A glaive grown from Hellgrowth, its blade still warm to the touch.

Cut from raw biomass before it could thicken into a hive's nervous tissue, and bound in iron to keep it from rooting again.

The Order's smiths burn the binding salts each dawn; on the days they forget, the blade is found longer than the day before.

A great axe forged in Velchoria's harbor districts, sized for whaling crews.

They hunted the leviathans of the Vulken Sea before the leviathans stopped surfacing.

The axes remain in the rafters of the old whale-houses; the smiths who reforge them say the steel smells of the deep while they cool.

A halberd whose hooked blade is forged in the silhouette of a waning moon.

The crescent predates the Lunitarian Church; smiths who still strike it into steel work in private, and only by commission from buyers who do not write their names down.

A heavy spiked mace, swung for the breaking of plate and the men inside it.

A Velchorian sergeant's favorite when the line breaks; the spikes catch on shield-rims and pull them down in a way an edged weapon will not.

A hefty broadsword wielded by Dragon Assassins.

Slaying dragons is a time honored service in the Velchorian Empire.

Historically taken up by humans, now predominantly pursued by Nephilim.

A hefty broadsword wielded by the Nephilim Paladins of the Order of the Crimson Moon.

The armaments of the Order take advantage of the Nephilim's innate strength, leveraging weight and durability that would be a hindrance for mortal man.

A long bone-pale staff cut, by tradition, from the wing of the Angel Azrael.

The Order's smiths refuse to repair them. When the staff cracks, the bearer is buried with it; when the bearer falls, the staff goes into the catacombs.

A long ceremonial staff carried by Cardinals of the Lunitarian Church, hafted for both rite and reach.

Cardinal Mathias carried his into the Archspire Cathedral on the night Solomon's vampires walked through the doors he had unlocked himself.

A long-hafted halberd carried by the foot soldiers of Eden's vampire clans.

The blades are sharpened to draw blood quickly and the staves grooved to drink it; vampires who must fight in the open prefer their kills tidy.

A long-hafted poleaxe of Order issue, the head stamped with the Crimson Concordat sigil.

Forged for Nephilim reach and Nephilim weight; mortal men have tried to take them from the dead, and have not lasted long carrying them.

A long-hafted weapon, head and haft fitted by whatever smithy the bearer could find that day.

Most of Eden's polearms outlive their hafts. The hafts are replaced again. And again.

A longsword belonging to an Infernal Legionnaire.

Demons of the Infernal Legion wield crude accursed weaponry imbued with dark magick.

A longsword issued to the Sovereign Sentries of the Velchorian throne.

The Sentries answer to the imperial crown and not the Church.

The distinction is small in peacetime… not so in war.

A magnificent weapon forged in honor of Gildenarch.

The magnificant rams of the Treveyan Highlands have long inspired the city of Gildenarch since the days before the city's founding.

No matter what changes, some truth yet remains.

A noble's hunting glaive, its socket cast as a dragon's mouth and the red gem set as its eye.

Carried in the deer-parks of the Velchorian high estates, where the only dragons left in Eden are the ones smiths still remember well enough to shape.

A poleaxe fashioned from a harvest scythe, the curve hammered straight and the haft re-bound in iron.

The peasants of the Velchorian inlands used them for planting.

Some still smell of the wheat they once cut.

A short-hafted war-hammer issued to Velchorian line infantry.

Made by the same forges that strike the Crusader Longsword, in lower grade and at higher volume.

The men who carry them outnumber the men who carry swords by roughly five to one.

A smoldering blade wielded by the extinct Mahkten Marrauders. Bestial warriors in service to The Lord of Perdition.

In times of old, when the Coil was yet whole, war dominated the lands of Eden, and none were more adept than Mahkteah's devoted.

A standard-issue broadsword carried by Velchorian footmen and freeholders.

Forged at the foundries of Sadrys and Belwayne in army-quantities.

Most men of Eden hold one in their first battle, and a fair number carry one through their last.

A sword wielded by Covenant Clerics, elite knights of the Lunitarian Covenant Crusaders.

It is expected for chaplains to be adept in combat as well as theology.

Masters of warfare both physical and spiritual.

A two-handed warhammer scaled and weighted for Nephilim hands.

The Order's smiths mark the haft for each demon the head has put down.

The hammers with the most marks are rarely returned with their wielder.

A wicked blade wielded by the demonic footsoldiers of the Infernal Lost Legion.

The blade looks as if it will perish after serving its usefulness. The legion wastes nothing in their conquests, for they have nothing left to lose.

An accursed sword once thought to be lost to legend.

The Revenant of Gildeus haunted the depths of Gildenarch.

Watching over the forgotten dead buried under the Church's occupation.

An ancient sword imbued with the Divine's holy moonlight. Its edge delivers immense Holy damage.

This blade's original bearer has been lost to history yet its identity and purpose remains clear.

The full moon cuts through darkness.

An ancient sword integral to Lunitarian history, both feared and respected.

The sword Axiom symbolized Lunitarian dominance and the eradication of paganism.

Its namesake is an assertion of the new world order that followed the War of the Gods.

An ancient worn blade corrupted by abyssal magick. It's essence pierces the very soul of its foes, bypassing most defenses.

The Seekers, devotees in service to Aegoroth, were blind scholars who dwelled in the deep dark beneath the lands.

An inquisitor's flamberge, its crossguard wrought into a thorn-halo around a single drop of red glass.

Carried by the Pyresworn, a Lunitarian inquisitorial order tasked with the burning of heretics by sentence and the burning of villages by mistake.

The red glass is said to hold a tear of the saint who founded them.

An unusual broadsword imbued with a fire enchantment.

Although heavily regulated by the Church, enchantments are among the most common forms of magick allowed within the Adamaic Empire.
Behold the legendary of Axe of The Gods. Forged from the heaviest of metals, and wielded by only the most brutal of warriors.

The Lunar Sentinels harken to a time before Lunarin's ascendance to the Divine Throne.

Any mentions of Lunarin worship before the Church are considered a vile heresy.

Attracting great skepticism and condemnation towards anyone seeking to revive ancient knowledge... now considered outdated.

The standard-issued imperial longsword, wielded by the Covenant Crusaders.

The Covenant Crusader is the enforcer of the Lunitarian Church's will, and is infamous across Eden for their passion and zealotry.

Designed for effective thrusting and is moderately useful for slashing.

The sword of Clan Telvaught.

Few tales do justice to the feuds between Eden's vampire clans than that of Clan Moore's seizure of Telvaught's legendary Scirax.

Taken from the corpse of Lord Erington.
